//: Type-checks the browser sources (npm run check:js). Nothing is emitted:
Node runs the TypeScript sources by stripping their types, the dev server
(scripts/dev-server.ts) strips them per request with esbuild, and
scripts/build-dist.ts bundles them with esbuild. That is why
erasableSyntaxOnly and verbatimModuleSyntax are on: a file must mean the same
thing once its types are blanked out, so no enums, namespaces or parameter
properties, and an import used only as a type says import type, or a strip
would leave a runtime import of a name that does not exist. Relative imports
name the .ts file, because Node resolves a specifier as written and never
maps .js to .ts; allowImportingTsExtensions (which needs noEmit) is what lets
tsc accept that. Node's types are left out on purpose so browser code cannot
lean on Node globals (setTimeout returning a Timeout, Buffer, process);
scripts/tsconfig.json adds them for the tooling, and check:js runs both
projects.
Target ES2022: the app needs Web Serial, WebUSB or Web Bluetooth, so it runs on
Chromium (Web Serial since 89), and every Chromium that can clone also has JSPI
(137+). strictNullChecks is on (2026-10-09; it found 203 errors here and 52
in scripts/): a value that can be null is typed T|null and checked, and a
null-initialised variable says what it will hold. noImplicitAny came next
(2026-10-09; 1097 errors across both projects once the sources were
TypeScript): every parameter says what it takes, and an explicit any is
kept to the places data arrives untyped. With those paid for, strict is on:
the rest of it cost 31 fixes, all useUnknownInCatchVariables, a caught value
being read through errorFields() (web/js/error-details.ts) because anything
can be thrown. The three flags below strict are checks it does not include.
